description: Machine-readable inventory of dependency-health audit checks for validation and generated maps.

statusTaxonomy.present: The expected invariant is fully satisfied.
statusTaxonomy.partial: Most signals resolve, with a small number of exceptions, or the codebase shows mixed adherence to a soft check.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete dependency state breaks the invariant.

enrichmentFlags.description: Enrich findings with registry data such as latest versions, deprecation flags, and publish dates.

relatedAudits.relationship: Owns whether the vulnerability scan and license check run as gates.
Owns application-level security; this audit owns supply-chain and dependency vulnerabilities.

checks.title: No high or critical vulnerabilities
checks.expectation: The package manager's audit reports no high or critical advisories.
checks.violationSignal: Any high or critical advisory, reported with package, severity, advisory ID, and fix availability.

checks.title: No moderate vulnerabilities
checks.expectation: The package manager's audit reports no moderate advisories.
checks.violationSignal: Moderate advisories present.

checks.title: Lockfile present and committed
checks.expectation: A lockfile exists and is tracked by git.
checks.violationSignal: No lockfile, or the lockfile is in .gitignore.

checks.title: Lockfile integrity verifiable
checks.expectation: The lockfile carries integrity hashes and continuous integration uses the frozen-install variant.
checks.violationSignal: A lockfile format without integrity hashes, or continuous-integration scripts not using the frozen-install variant.

checks.title: No install scripts from untrusted packages
checks.expectation: Direct dependencies that declare lifecycle scripts are limited to a known-trusted allowlist.
checks.violationSignal: Direct-dependency lifecycle scripts from packages outside the allowlist, reported with the package, the script, and the script body.

checks.title: Continuous-integration vulnerability scanning enabled
checks.expectation: A continuous-integration workflow runs the package manager's audit, or Dependabot, Snyk, or Renovate configuration is present.
checks.violationSignal: No such automation detected.

checks.title: No dependencies more than two majors behind
checks.expectation: Each direct dependency is at most the threshold number of major versions behind its latest release.
checks.violationSignal: A direct dependency exceeds the threshold, reported with current and latest.

checks.title: No deprecated-major usage
checks.expectation: No direct dependency runs on an upstream-deprecated major version.
checks.violationSignal: Deprecated-major usage.

checks.title: No abandoned packages
checks.expectation: No direct dependency has gone more than the threshold months without a publish.
checks.violationSignal: Direct dependencies whose latest publish is older than the threshold.

checks.title: No officially deprecated packages
checks.expectation: No direct dependency carries a deprecated flag in the registry.
checks.violationSignal: A deprecated direct dependency, reported with the deprecation message and recommended replacement.

checks.title: Peer dependencies satisfied
checks.expectation: Every declared peer dependency in the tree resolves to a satisfying version.
checks.violationSignal: Unsatisfied peer dependency warnings from the package manager's list command.

checks.title: Every package has a license declared
checks.expectation: No package in the dependency tree is missing a license field.
checks.violationSignal: Packages with UNLICENSED, an unresolvable SEE LICENSE IN reference, or a missing field.

checks.title: Strong-copyleft licenses are flagged for human review
checks.expectation: The audit surfaces GPL, AGPL, or LGPL packages for human review, passing them only when an allowlist file includes them.
checks.violationSignal: GPL, AGPL, or LGPL in the tree with no allowlist file.

checks.title: Source-available restrictive licenses are flagged for human review
checks.expectation: The audit surfaces SSPL, BUSL, Commons Clause, or similar for human review, passing them only when an allowlist file includes them.
checks.violationSignal: Restrictive licenses present without an allowlist.

checks.title: License-checker tool present
checks.expectation: A license-enforcement tool is configured and a continuous-integration step runs it.
checks.violationSignal: No license tool detected, or a tool present without a continuous-integration step invoking it.

checks.title: No unused dependencies
checks.expectation: Every entry in dependencies and devDependencies is imported somewhere in the project.
checks.violationSignal: Packages declared but never imported; the finding records the confidence level.

checks.title: No misplaced dependencies
checks.expectation: Production packages live in dependencies and development-only packages live in devDependencies.
checks.violationSignal: A devDependency imported by production code, or a dependency imported only by test or build files.

checks.title: No duplicate packages
checks.expectation: Each package appears at exactly one resolved version in the lockfile.
checks.violationSignal: The same package name at multiple versions in the lockfile.

checks.title: No package-manager mixing
checks.expectation: Exactly one lockfile is present and continuous integration uses the same package manager that produced it.
checks.violationSignal: Multiple lockfiles, or a workflow using a different package manager than the lockfile implies.

checks.title: Security-critical packages exact-pinned
checks.expectation: A configurable allowlist of security-critical packages is exact-pinned in package.json.
checks.violationSignal: Security-critical packages declared with a caret or tilde range.

checks.title: engines field declared
checks.expectation: package.json declares the supported node version range.
checks.violationSignal: The engines field is absent.
